# Secretary desktop · PhaseUI

macOS Tauri 2 / Svelte desktop. PhaseUI (#62) presents the existing FE-02 Core workflow in the frozen v1.0 three-column shell. The [Current Frontend Spec](../frontend/README.md) is the single design and acceptance entry. Normal launch opens the connected workflow; `SECRETARY_STUDY=1` opens the synthetic FE-00 study. Linux desktop implementation and acceptance are deferred; existing Core Linux CI is unchanged.

## PhaseUI components and diagnostics

Ordinary launch opens Conversation. Connection controls are in the top Connection dialog; Tasks contains existing task/results, Pending contains approvals/outbox. Other destinations are named empty slots owned by #63–#66. The activity rail exists only on Conversation. Theme and motion preferences use `secretary.phaseui.v1.*`; production defaults to BASE, while EXTENDED remains an experiment.

The [component contract](../../../src/secretary_desktop/src/phaseui/README.md) documents imports, states, ownership and consumer examples. Geometry follows frozen design `8cdb921`; default/long names use a 22px brand size to fit Secretary in the 196px sidebar, an explicit adaptation from the prototype's short PERRI label. Core and client defaults are Secretary; explicit lowercase names retain their spelling.

Opt into the gallery or the isolated production-shell benchmark in the same Release binary:

```sh
SECRETARY_PHASEUI_SCENARIO=gallery 'src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/Secretary Study.app/Contents/MacOS/secretary-desktop-spike'
python3 scripts/phaseui_measure.py --scenario single --mode all --rounds 3
python3 scripts/phaseui_measure.py --scenario all --mode all --rounds 3
python3 scripts/phaseui_measure.py --scenario idle --mode all --rounds 3 --uninstrumented
```

Selectors: gallery, idle, single, navigation, input-scroll, stream-stress, bridge-cadence. Modes: off/base/extended; seed: unsigned 32-bit integer. Conflicting legacy selectors and invalid values fail explicitly. Diagnostic launch does not open the real profile/store or start a Core worker. Gallery offers frozen frames, schemes, extension toggles, text size and native window width/zoom. The measurement harness injects an in-memory BridgePort into Connected. Stress uses 20Hz/1200 updates; bridge-cadence simulates the existing 1500ms snapshot/250ms transient schedule and does not measure network latency. A separate real-bridge fixture suite verifies integration.

Measurements use one ordinary Release hash, three repeats per mode/scenario, 60 seconds active and 30 seconds recovery (idle first settles 30 seconds). rAF delay is a callback proxy; sampled computed visibility is a logical frame proxy, not physical display proof. Controller counters cover owned resources only. New WebKit processes are attribution candidates; existing shared processes are reported separately. Ordinary Release has no Web Inspector; paint/GPU remains NOT_TESTED. Master performs final aesthetic/performance acceptance. Linux desktop remains NOT_TESTED.

## Historical FE-00 study

The Run, native study checklist and legacy measure commands below describe the retained FE-00 study. Its green sample, streaming virtualization and evidence are separate from PhaseUI. Launch it explicitly with `SECRETARY_STUDY=1`.

## Run

Requires macOS, Xcode command-line tools, Node 22.22+, and Rust 1.97.1 (`rustup`, see rust-toolchain.toml). From this directory:

```sh
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
npm ci
npm run check
npm test
npm run tauri -- build
open 'src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/Secretary Study.app'
```

`npm run tauri -- dev` uses a local Vite development server. Ordinary Release embeds static assets and opens no listening server. In study mode, Rust exposes a whitelisted study configuration, a one-time ready marker, and bounded JSON metrics to its own stdout when explicitly launched by the measurement harness. The ordinary UI has no recurring frame sampler or telemetry IPC; instrumented streaming and the native-test build enable frame sampling. No Core tokens, file access, shell execution, external navigation or remote assets are available to the page. Capability permissions are scoped to `main`: zoom, those three measurement commands, and the restricted FE-01 bridge commands.

Use **Validation tools** (`验证工具`) at the bottom of the directory for fixtures, streaming, frame-by-frame replay, reduced motion, full-DOM baseline, and native WebView zoom. The default reading view recycles offscreen message contents. Starting text selection retains document contents until selection clears; this intentionally trades selection-time memory for native cross-message selection. Full-DOM baseline is a separate comparison mode. It is not evidence that recycling passed.

Code blocks are plain pre/code without syntax highlighting. Markdown disables raw HTML, images, and clickable links. The stream updates the growing message rather than rebuilding historical messages. During document selection its displayed projection freezes while data continues arriving; clearing selection catches up. Closing the window affects only this spike.

## Native automation and evidence

The `native-test` Rust feature and separate Tauri configuration add the embedded WDIO server only to a test binary in `target/native-test`. Never use that binary for resource baselines or distribution. Build with `npm run build:native` (Rust on PATH), then run `npm run test:native`. `npm run test:native` tests WKWebView, not Chrome. Synthetic keyboard/composition tests are labeled as such and never replace system IME tests.

`npm run evidence -- window|selection|phase|motion|security` creates an immutable run directory under repository `.demo-data/issue58/runs/`. `npm run evidence -- ime` creates a NOT_TESTED record until the native manual cases below are performed. The window/selection/phase/motion aliases run the complete native suite, with the requested focus recorded separately in invocation.json; they do not claim an isolated manual case. A successful script is not automatically a product GO; read the case status and the acceptance report.

## Manual Mac acceptance

Run the ordinary Release, record binary SHA and native window owner PID. Capture only the study window, not personal desktop contents. Screen capture may require the existing macOS screen-recording permission.

- Window: close/reopen, minimize/restore, drag, narrow/wide resize. Tab/Shift-Tab and mouse must reach the input and buttons. At 100/125/150/200% WebView zoom, paragraphs and controls remain usable; code can scroll horizontally.
- Real IME: select the system Pinyin input source, use the fixed text `中文，English。` and repeat each case three times: Enter confirms a candidate, Space selects, Escape cancels, click Send during composition, switch windows during composition, confirm then quickly press an independent Enter, compose while stream runs. Candidate confirmation/cancellation/focus loss must not send. A committed independent send must preserve the exact text and occur once. The recent-events panel records event order and decisions. Export/capture logs with only synthetic text.
- Selection: load 1,000 records, drag from message 10 to 900 and in reverse, including long code; copy/paste into a plain-text editor and compare with the document text. Test body Cmd+A separately from textarea Cmd+A, selection during 5 seconds of streaming, and selection across insertion of 200 previous messages. No silent truncation or focus/scroll takeover.
- Phase: capture frame 0 and frames 1/2/3, plus natural playback. The three horizontal slices use the same path and move independently. Input text, caret and hit areas stay fixed. Master evaluates the actual window.
- Reduced motion: while paused at frame 2 or playing, enable the application switch and then separately the system Reduce Motion option. Both restore the intact neutral icon, with stable focus/layout.

For an observing-only recorder, use `STUDY_MANUAL=1 npm run test:native`; operate the real system IME and window yourself. It records native events without synthesizing composition and stops after ten minutes. Confirm the input source by observing Chinese candidate commit before counting a run; English autocorrection is not IME evidence.

A missing manual result stays NOT_TESTED. Master visual approval cannot be supplied by automation.

## Measure ordinary Release

```sh
npm run measure -- --scenario startup --rounds 10
npm run measure -- --scenario idle
npm run measure -- --scenario stream
npm run measure -- --scenario idle --uninstrumented
npm run measure -- --scenario stream --baseline
```

The harness starts only its own binary and terminates only the process it created. It writes an immutable `index.json`, CPU/RSS samples and UI summaries. Startup: first launch plus ten warm launches, monotonic spawn-to-ready including marker delivery. Idle: 30 seconds settling + 60 seconds sampling. Stream: nominal 20 updates/s for 1,200 updates; wait for actual completion and queue drain, then observe 30 seconds recovery (180-second total deadline; insufficient recovery fails even if updates finish). The harness temporarily prevents sleep with caffeinate scoped to its app PID; it restores this condition on exit. Instrumented runs include 1Hz metrics IPC and streaming frame sampling; the reporting-off idle control disables both; input bookkeeping and a periodic callback remain. Full-DOM baseline retains all message markup with content-visibility; it is a separate comparison. CPU is cumulative user/kernel time difference; 100% means one logical CPU. PID identity uses launch time, with appearance/exit records; CPU deltas are discarded across identity changes. Sampler wall time and unavailable refresh/thermal fields are explicit. WebKit XPC candidates and preexisting shared processes are separate, not falsely attributed via the parent PID. RSS sums can double-count shared memory. Capture footage separately from performance sampling.

See the repository `docs/fix/` plan and `docs/fix/evidence/issue58-feasibility/summary.md` for exact results and remaining gates. No Linux desktop result is claimed.

## FE-01 native Core bridge (macOS)

Normal startup shows the real connection UI; `SECRETARY_STUDY=1` retains the synthetic FE-00 study. Their evidence is kept separate.
WebView exposes only named `bridge_*` commands, with no Core token, general file, URL, or shell IPC.

Create `profiles.json` in the macOS application-data directory `~/Library/Application Support/dev.secretary.study/`, with directory mode 0700 and file mode 0600. Example (replace with your absolute paths):

```json
[{"id":"local-fixture","data_dir":"/absolute/private/fixture-core","expected_mode":"fixture","node_abs":"/absolute/bin/node","core_root":"/absolute/Secretary","backend_entry":"/absolute/Secretary/src/pi_secretary/src/backend.ts"}]
```

Run `npm ci` in core_root first. Native start always launches the fixture backend with explicit cwd/SECRETARY_DATA/SECRETARY_MODE; Finder startup does not rely on shell cwd/PATH. For live profiles use `expected_mode: "live"`, start the live wrapper using the Core operations guide, then attach. Closing the client does not stop Core; stopping requires separate confirmation. Missing configuration or invalid permissions produce an error; other data directories are never guessed.

When changing data_domain, create a new profile ID and restart the client. Preserve the old profile database and unresolved commands; no database deletion is needed.

Each profile has a separate `client.sqlite` (WAL/FULL, schema version 1). Drafts, reading anchors, original commands, and receipts persist in the native database; tokens never persist. One transaction saves the outbox and clears the matching draft version. After send failure, query the receipt first and resend with the same ID/content. `ACCEPTED` means admission only; related projections show business outcomes. UNKNOWN, a lost admitted receipt, or authentication/data-domain conflicts block automatic resend. stop binds the current instance and is never retried automatically.

The cache retains at most 16 subscription windows; switching subscriptions atomically clears old projections. Temporary next-page responses do not accumulate in persistent cache. Each change refreshes current subscriptions; data and applied cursor commit together, with serial refreshes preventing stale overwrite. SSE bounded-queue overflow disconnects; the same sync/changes path catches up from the persisted watermark. transient retains only the latest in-memory snapshot. Budgets: cache 64 MiB/10,000 items; response 2 MiB; sync queue 512 KiB; command 1 MiB; outbox 1,000 items/32 MiB; drafts 16 MiB; downloads 256 MiB. Intent quota exhaustion preserves the draft and reports an error. Admitted records remain 30 days; unresolved records are never automatically deleted.

Types and the operation catalog are generated from the existing API schema: `npm run contracts:generate` / `npm run contracts:check`. The fixed allowlist is in `scripts/bridge-operations.json`; admin/push, settings writes, and scope writes are excluded by default. Extending the bridge requires extending both its explicit operation subset and regression coverage.

Validation commands:

```sh
npm run contracts:check
npm run check && npm test
cargo fmt --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --check
cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --test-threads=1
npm run build:native
node scripts/bridge-fixture.mjs
SECRETARY_DESKTOP_TEST_DATA=/absolute/Secretary/.demo-data/issue59-native BRIDGE_TEST=1 npm run test:native
```

Rust integration tests launch real fixture Core, HTTP/SSE, and persistent Store. SIGKILL subtests are workers explicitly launched by parent tests; being individually marked ignored does not mean kill acceptance was skipped. Native tests use isolated profiles; release ignores test-configuration overrides and excludes WDIO. Linux desktop remains NOT_TESTED; Core Linux CI is unchanged.

Draft persistence uses a separate SQLite connection and is not blocked by the network-sync lock. Command-list snapshots show at most 50 entries with 2048-character body previews; full original intents remain in the database. The OS releases each profile’s delivery-file lock on exit/crash.

Current FE-01 limits: draft writes are independent of the network lock, but send and snapshots still serialize with sync and may wait one request timeout (10 seconds) if Core does not respond. Snapshots return full projections for active windows; FE-02 should select windows per page to avoid frequent full rendering of large windows. Receipts over 64 KiB persist only as summaries; full details are queryable through the unified bridge at `requests/{id}`, but the current validation UI has no dedicated full-receipt view. SYNCED means persisted data has caught up, not continuous availability of the transient preview channel.

## Conversation and unified timeline (FE-04)

Thinking is enabled by default. Thinking bodies and tool-call details start collapsed and can be expanded; collapsed entries show only a summary. Turning thinking off immediately clears its presentation and memory cache. The display preference is saved per data domain.

History supports paging in both directions, message or event ID lookup, and search within the loaded window. At most 3 pages and 150 rows are resident, with 8 MiB for text and thinking and 2 MiB per expanded message. Following occurs only while already at the tail without a text selection. Sending does not force a jump; use “Go to latest messages” explicitly.

Full copy is offered only after the loaded body reaches EOF; otherwise the action explicitly copies the loaded portion. Links require explicit address inspection and opening and allow HTTP/HTTPS only. Remote images display alt text only.

The related rail changes scope only on explicit selection; reads send no viewed/presented/read commands. The attention page provides paginated access to full original unresolved or failed messages. Copying or restoring does not resend, and restoration cannot overwrite an existing draft. Failed messages are protected from local quota eviction and cleanup; only confirmed failed records whose text has been recovered may be explicitly discarded.

When the session enters RECOVERY_BLOCKED, the client offers a confirmed “Resume session” action using the existing session/resume command and original request-receipt protocol to continue unfinished turns. Accepted messages are not resubmitted.

Message projections may include source kind, original event ID, direct related IDs, outcome, and preview availability, derived only from existing records. A saved preview is not durable success; expired previews report no final record.
